data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's mechanism claims the checklist 'externalizes the stable' high-variance cognitive operations constituting expert competence, but it never addresses the problem's central requirement: identifying evidence within a single evaluation that distinguishes genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance tracking the right answer. Its counterconditions mention checklist failure modes, but none of them surface an observable diagnostic usable in one evaluation to separate genuine competence from rote compliance that happens to match the correct answer on in-distribution items.
